steps._comment: Exactly four shown events: open, Moon Bone equip, Stonescale equip, Moon Bone unequip. Cursor moves and refusal/tool toasts must not replay the panel chime.

== (7) GH#334 note 1: THE DRAG-TO-SCROLL LEG == the 19-item pack is the only place in the game where the carried list is genuinely taller than its viewport, so this is where the gesture has to be proven. Before this wave the list had NO touch/drag handling at all: on touch, Godot's touch->mouse emulation turned the first contact into a left-button PRESS that `_confirm()` acted on instantly, so a swipe to read past the fold equipped whatever row the finger started on. Setup: two move_downs wrap the cursor 17 -> 18 -> 0, and `_rebuild_items`' cursor==0 branch snaps the scroll back to the top, giving the drag somewhere to go.
steps.name: move_down

steps._comment: Drag UP inside the list (70% -> 25% of its height) = scroll DOWN, journal_body's own sign convention. Two things must follow: the viewport actually moved, and the CURSOR came with it (note 1(b) -- the wheel used to move the viewport while `> `, the detail column and the mechanical corner all kept describing an item that was now off screen, and the next arrow press threw the scroll away re-snapping to the stale cursor). The forward-only wait below is the cursor-follow proof: it can only match a selection emitted AFTER the {cursor:0} wait above, i.e. one the drag itself caused.
The drag must not confirm an item. Before the separate physical-full leg, only Moon Bone/Stonescale equips and Moon Bone unequip are legitimate.
Inventory echoes the refusal immediately; the global toast queue renders it after the modal closes.
